# Two-shape coefficients and the discrete-base Green cone
statements for a Minkowski-affine chain of positive-dimensional
polytopal fibers. They do not assert that an arbitrary depth minimizer
is polytopal, has a fixed fan, or is a Minkowski-affine chain. They give
no universal favorable sign for the displayed depth responses.

The finite support cone itself was established in
support-array-cone-and-minkowski-obstruction.md. The new structural
calculation here is its explicit factorization, at an affine chain,
by the Dirichlet Green kernel in the DISCRETE INTEGER BASE, including
the endpoint tangent cones and lineality. This is distinct from the
earlier continuous-angle Green kernels for planar curvature.
The resulting inequalities specialize existing support and concave-roof
tests; they are not asserted to be stronger than all such tests.

## 1. Exact compatibility of two-shape coefficients

Let P be a finite complete lattice base and A,B compact convex bodies
in the continuous space. For numbers theta_p in [0,1] put

    K_p=(1-theta_p)A+theta_p B,    Delta(u)=h_B(u)-h_A(u).

The prescribed fibers are the actual fibers of their convex hull if
and only if, for every anchored representation
q=sum_p lambda_p p with lambda_p>=0 and sum_p lambda_p=1,

    (theta_q-sum_p lambda_p theta_p) Delta(u)>=0
                                                     (1)

for every continuous normal u. Indeed the required Minkowski inclusion
sum_p lambda_p K_p subset K_q is equivalent to its support inequalities,
which simplify to (1). These inclusions are sufficient because every
point of the hull at integer base q is such a convex combination.
Completeness ensures that the hull has no additional integer bases.

In particular:

* If A and B are nonnested, Delta takes both signs, so (1) holds
  exactly when theta preserves every anchored representation.
* If A is a proper subset of B, (1) is exactly sampled concavity
  theta_q>=sum lambda_p theta_p.
* If B is a proper subset of A, the inequalities are reversed.
* If A=B, all coefficients give the same family.

On P={0,...,N}, preservation of every anchored representation is
equivalent to theta_j being affine in j: consecutive midpoint
equalities force this, and affine functions preserve all barycenters.
Thus a proposed exchange in a fixed nonnested two-shape span cannot
choose its coefficients independently at different integer bases.
This statement concerns actual support compatibility, not merely
concavity of fiber volumes.

## 2. The fan space and its finite support inequalities

Fix N>=2 and full-dimensional polytopes A,B in R^d, d>=1. Set

    K_j=(1-j/N)A+(j/N)B,       j=0,...,N.

Let F be the normal fan of A+B, the common refinement of the normal
fans F_A,F_B. Every interior K_j has exactly fan F. To see this, the
exposed face of a positive Minkowski sum is the sum of the two exposed
faces; its normal cones are precisely the common intersections of the
two normal fans. Positive coefficients change neither these cones nor
their incidence.

Choose one nonzero vector r on each ray of F, and denote their finite
set by R. Let V_F be the vector space of continuous homogeneous
functions linear on every cone of F. Its coordinates may be taken as
values on R, subject to the linear consistency conditions on
nonsimplicial cones. For d=2 there are no such conditions: two
independent boundary rays determine each linear piece.

If f belongs to V_F and sigma is a maximal cone, let ell_sigma be
its linear piece on sigma. Then f is a convex support function if
and only if

    f(r)-ell_sigma(r)>=0     for every sigma and every r in R.   (2)

Necessity follows from the supporting linear piece. Conversely,
(2), extended by nonnegative combinations of rays on each cone,
gives ell_sigma(u)<=f(u) everywhere. On its own cone a piece
equals f. Hence f=max_sigma ell_sigma is finite and convex,
and is the support function of the convex hull of these finitely
many linear-piece vectors.

For the support function h of a polytope whose fan is exactly F,
the inequalities in (2) are strict whenever r is outside sigma.
For r in sigma they are identities throughout V_F. This follows
also because equality means that the vertex corresponding to sigma
is exposed at r, exactly the condition r belongs to its normal cone.
Consequently every sufficiently small perturbation of h in V_F
remains a support function with this same fan. Full dimension
persists by uniform convergence of support functions.

For a possibly coarser endpoint fan define T_A^F by imposing, on
eta in V_F, the nonnegative versions of the rows in (2) which are
active at h_A. Then

    eta belongs to T_A^F
       iff h_A+t eta is a support function for all sufficiently
           small t>=0.                                    (3)

The inactive rows remain positive for small t, and the active rows
are exactly t times their values on eta. Define T_B^F identically.
These are explicit finite polyhedral tangent cones.

Finally write

    C_F={c in V_F: c(u)>=0 for all u}
       ={c in V_F: c(r)>=0 for every r in R}.              (4)

The second equality follows cone by cone. This cone is pointed.
In dimension two it is the nonnegative orthant in ray coordinates;
in higher dimensions the consistency equations must be retained.

## 3. Exact Green decomposition, including endpoint motions

For 1<=i,j<=N-1 define

    G_ji=min(i,j)(N-max(i,j))/N.                          (5)

Set G_0i=G_Ni=0. For an array delta_j in V_F define

    c_i=2 delta_i-delta_(i-1)-delta_(i+1).                (6)

**Theorem 1.** The arrays h_j+t delta_j are support functions of
full-dimensional actual fibers on {0,...,N}, for all sufficiently
small t>=0, if and only if

    eta_0:=delta_0 belongs to T_A^F,
    eta_N:=delta_N belongs to T_B^F,
    c_i belongs to C_F for every 1<=i<=N-1.              (7)

Every such array has the unique representation

    delta_j=(1-j/N)eta_0+(j/N)eta_N
                         +sum_(i=1)^(N-1) G_ji c_i.    (8)

**Proof.** Support realizability at the endpoints is (3). All interior
support functions have the full fan F, so Section 2 gives support
realizability for every sufficiently small interior perturbation.
There are finitely many fibers, so one common positive time works.

For a fixed u, the original sequence h_j(u) is affine in j.
The perturbed sequence is concave exactly when all its consecutive
second differences are nonnegative, namely when t c_i(u)>=0.
Consecutive concavity is equivalent to all anchored concavity
inequalities on an integer interval: the piecewise affine
interpolant has nonincreasing slopes and is concave, so Jensen's
inequality applies to every convex representation of an integer
base. Conversely adjacent midpoint representations are required.
Thus (7) is exactly actual compatibility, by the support argument
of Section 1. Ray tests suffice by (4).

The kernel satisfies

    2G_ji-G_(j-1)i-G_(j+1)i=1 if j=i, and 0 otherwise.

This follows directly by subtracting the two affine branches in
(5); at i the two slopes differ by one. Formula (8) consequently
has the specified endpoints and second differences. Their
difference from any other solution has zero second differences
and zero endpoints, and therefore vanishes. The hull has projection
[0,N], precisely the prescribed integer bases, and is a compact
full-dimensional convex body. This proves the theorem.

For fixed endpoints, (8) reduces to a sum of nonnegative Green
modes. Since G_ji>0 for all interior i,j, a nonzero curvature
in one normal direction changes every interior fiber's support
in that direction. In particular, fixed endpoints permit no
nonzero independent inward change. They do permit coupled
outward changes even if every independent enlargement reserve
is locked.

### Exact lineality

The lineality space of T_A^F is V_(F_A), embedded in V_F.
Indeed, if both eta and -eta are feasible at h_A, then on any cone
of F_A, where h_A is linear, eta and -eta are convex. Thus eta is
linear on that cone. Conversely a perturbation in V_(F_A) keeps
all identities of the old fan and preserves its finitely many
strict inequalities for both signs of sufficiently small t.
The same argument applies to B.

Since C_F is pointed, (8) shows that the full lineality consists
exactly of

    delta_j=(1-j/N)eta_0+(j/N)eta_N,
    eta_0 in V_(F_A), eta_N in V_(F_B).                 (9)

Thus free endpoint motions must not be omitted. When both endpoints
already have fan F, these two endpoint functions are arbitrary
elements of V_F. Translations and affine fiber shears are included,
but generally form only part of this lineality.

## 4. The locked triangle-to-square chain

Take N=3, A=conv(0,e_1,e_2), B=[0,1]^2. In the ray order

    -e_1, -e_2, e_1, e_2, e_1+e_2,

the common fan has five rays. The two interior fibers are genuine
pentagons, and fixed-endpoint motions are exactly

    delta_1(r)=(2c_1(r)+c_2(r))/3,
    delta_2(r)=(c_1(r)+2c_2(r))/3,
    c_1(r),c_2(r)>=0.                                  (10)

There are ten elementary modes. Equivalently
2delta_1(r)>=delta_2(r) and 2delta_2(r)>=delta_1(r).
If either support velocity is positive, their ratio is between
1/2 and 2; if either is zero, both are zero.

For clarity the endpoint tangent constraints can also be written
explicitly. Use X,Y,S,-X,-Y for the five support coordinates.
At the triangle endpoint the only nontrivial active fan conditions
on eta_0 are

    eta_0(S)-eta_0(X)+eta_0(-Y)>=0,
    eta_0(S)-eta_0(Y)+eta_0(-X)>=0.                     (11)

They say that the vertical and horizontal edges born at (1,0)
and (0,1) have nonnegative length. At the square endpoint the
only such condition is

    eta_N(X)+eta_N(Y)-eta_N(S)>=0.                      (12)

It says that the diagonal cut at the top-right vertex has
nonnegative length. The other three, respectively four, edge
lengths are already positive. Thus (11)--(12), together with
the ten conditions (6)>=0, describe the full twenty-dimensional
tangent cone in these coordinates. Its lineality has dimension
3+4=7, as also follows from (9).

An explicit motion transverse to the original two-shape span
increases both X and Y supports of BOTH interior fibers by t,
keeps their diagonal supports fixed, and keeps the endpoints
fixed. In (10) this has c_1=c_2=1 for X,Y and zero on the other
three rays. It is therefore an actual deformation for all small
t>=0. The old two-shape interpolation changes only diagonal
support, so this motion is outside that span.

The source candidate 34d8ea3ce4f23a92
proves that all four independent enlargement reserves are locked;
its independent audit is
audit-all-fibers-locked-minkowski-chain-coherent.md.
The present calculation supplies coupled motions at that exact
family. It asserts no favorable depth response for them.

## 5. Exact first variations and elementary mass constants

For an interior fiber j and ray r, let F_jr be its facet with
outward normal r, and set

    a_jr=H_(d-1)(F_jr)/|r|.                             (13)

The support coordinate delta_j(r) is an offset velocity, so its
normal speed is delta_j(r)/|r|. Consequently

    M'=sum_(j,r) a_jr delta_j(r).                       (14)

For fixed endpoints the sum is over 1<=j<=N-1. The same formula
holds with endpoint facets included, assigning zero area to
missing endpoint facets. New zero-area facets contribute o(t).

For a fixed closed cap H and a fixed-endpoint Green-cone direction,
all support velocities are nonnegative. Define

    b_H,jr=|r|^(-1) integral_(F_jr) chi_H^+ dH_(d-1),
    chi_H^+(x)=lim_(s down to 0) 1_H(j,x+s r/|r|).      (15)

Then

    mu_t(H)=mu_0(H)+t sum_(j,r)b_H,jr delta_j(r)+o(t).   (16)

The limit in (15) exists. On a coincident cap boundary it is
one for an outward-oriented cap, zero for an inward-oriented
cap, and one when the continuous cap normal is zero. Thus (16)
retains pure-integer caps and closed boundary mass.

To justify (14)--(16), exhaust each facet by compact patches away
from its edges. Its swept strip has thickness
t delta_j(r)/|r|+o(t), and intersections of strips contribute o(t).
The remaining edge neighborhoods have arbitrarily small facet
measure with a uniformly O(t) swept thickness. Fubini and this
exhaustion prove the formulas. For signed endpoint or other
signed velocities, a coincident cap has the usual min/max
branch; the linear formula below is only used when coincidence
has been explicitly excluded.

In the planar case facet length divided by |r| is affine along
a Minkowski chain. Indeed the exposed edge of a Minkowski sum
is the sum of two parallel edges or points, whose lengths add.
Writing a=a_0r and b=a_Nr gives

    a_jr=(1-j/N)a+(j/N)b.

Direct summation of the two branches of (5) yields

    sum_j G_ji=i(N-i)/2,
    sum_j jG_ji=i(N-i)(N+i)/6.

Hence a single planar Green mode c_i(r)=1 has mass derivative

    i(N-i)[(2N-i)a+(N+i)b]/(6N).                       (17)

For the four-site example the values for i=1,2 are respectively

    r=-e_1 or -e_2:     1,   1;
    r= e_1 or  e_2:    4/9, 5/9;
    r= e_1+e_2:        5/9, 4/9.

In particular the transverse motion at the end of Section 4
has M'=2.

## 6. Regular critical circuits: the exact Green response

This section states a REGULAR PHASE. It does not silently exclude
active pure-integer caps at an arbitrary minimizer.

Let M=sum_j |K_j| and let the actual normalized maximum depth
be beta, with Q=beta M. At each deepest base p_g select a
finite group of caps

    H_gl={alpha_gl z+v_gl.x>=b_gl},    |v_gl|=1,
    mu_0(H_gl)=Q,

and positive numbers rho_gl such that

    sum_l rho_gl v_gl=0,
    sum_l rho_gl(b_gl-alpha_gl p_g)=0.                 (18)

These equalities imply that the caps cover the ENTIRE continuous
plane at base p_g: their weighted affine defining functions sum
to zero, so they cannot all be strictly negative. Assume every
other base has a fixed finite whole-plane cap cover with all
masses strictly below Q.

Assume each selected cap has a two-sided threshold expansion

    mu_0(H_gl(b_gl+s))=Q-S_gl s+o(|s|),   S_gl>0.      (19)

Assume also that its boundary has zero (d-1)-measure on every
facet whose velocity is being considered. To use the full
endpoint cone below, impose this on all original facets.
These assumptions exclude problematic facet coincidences in
the joint body/threshold variation. They do not assert that
all deepest bases always possess such circuits.

Define

    kappa_gl=(rho_gl/S_gl)/sum_l(rho_gl/S_gl),
    q_g,jr=sum_l kappa_gl b_Hgl,jr-beta a_jr.           (20)

For a regular signed direction, b in this formula is the
ordinary facet cap measure divided by |r|; there is no
coincidence ambiguity. For fixed-endpoint Green directions put

    R_gi(c)=sum_r [sum_j G_ji q_g,jr] c(r).            (21)

**Theorem 2.** For any c_i in C_F, the actual deformation in
Theorem 1, with fixed endpoints, satisfies

    limsup_(t down to 0) [D(K(t))-beta]/t
       <= M^(-1) max_g sum_i R_gi(c_i).                (22)

Thus strict negativity for every group gives actual descent.

**Proof.** Let A_gl be the fixed-cap derivative in (16), and set
T_g=sum_l kappa_gl A_gl. Move each cap threshold at speed

    dot b_gl=(A_gl-T_g)/S_gl.

Then sum_l rho_gl dot b_gl=0 by (20), so the full-plane cover
(18) persists exactly. The joint cap derivative is
A_gl-S_gl dot b_gl=T_g. The joint formula follows by combining
the threshold slab in (19) with the facet strips: their overlap
is o(t), since the intersection of the cap boundary with each
moving facet is null. Fixed slack covers stay below Q for small
t by continuity of their finitely many cap masses.

Every candidate point in every actual fiber is consequently in
a covering cap of mass at most Q+t max_g T_g+o(t). Dividing by
M+t M'+o(t) gives the upper derivative
M^(-1)max_g(T_g-beta M'). Equations (8), (14), and (20)
give (21)--(22). This proves the claim for every point, not
merely the selected centers.

At a local minimum relative to this deformation class, for EVERY
selected regular circuit system there exist pi_g>=0, sum_g pi_g=1,
such that

    sum_g pi_g R_gi(c)>=0
         for every i and every c in C_F.              (23)

Indeed otherwise the finite-dimensional cone of group responses
contains a vector with every coordinate negative, giving (22).
Separation from the open negative orthant supplies a nonzero
nonnegative separating vector pi; its homogeneity forces
nonnegativity on the whole response cone, and normalization
gives (23). The response cone is polyhedral because C_F is.

For planar fibers, (23) becomes the finite Green-potential test

    sum_j G_ji [sum_g pi_g q_g,jr]>=0
                  for every i and every ray r.        (24)

This detects the exact coupled response required by compatibility;
it is not legitimate to replace it by an independent sign test
at one locked fiber.

## 7. Free endpoints, lineality, and relation to roof tests

Under the same regularity assumptions on ALL original facets,
define the group linear response on the full cone by

    L_g(delta)=sum_(j=0)^N sum_r q_g,jr delta_j(r),     (25)

with zero area at missing endpoint facets. The proof of (22)
applies with sum_i R_gi replaced by L_g.
At a local minimum, separation on the FULL cone (7), rather
than only its fixed-endpoint subcone, gives one common pi
for which sum_g pi_g L_g is nonnegative on that full cone.
In addition to (23), it therefore vanishes on every lineality
direction (9), and is nonnegative on the endpoint tangent
cones. The pi supplied by the full-cone separation can differ
from one chosen using only fixed endpoints.

More explicitly, with q_jr=sum_g pi_g q_g,jr, the two endpoint
functionals act through the FULL interpolation sums

    H_0,r=sum_j(1-j/N)q_jr,    H_N,r=sum_j(j/N)q_jr.

Thus sum_r H_0,r eta_0(r)>=0 for eta_0 in T_A^F and
sum_r H_N,r eta_N(r)>=0 for eta_N in T_B^F. These are not
conditions on q_0r and q_Nr alone.

If A and B both have the full planar fan F, endpoint lineality
allows arbitrary values independently at each ray. Writing
q_jr=sum_g pi_g q_g,jr, its consequences are exactly

    sum_j q_jr=0,       sum_j j q_jr=0,                 (26)
    s_ir:=sum_(j=1)^(N-1)G_ji q_jr>=0.                (27)

Conversely (26)--(27) imply nonnegative aggregate response for
every compatible direction. Equivalently, with s_0r=s_Nr=0,

    q_jr=2s_jr-s_(j-1)r-s_(j+1)r  (1<=j<=N-1),
    q_0r=-s_1r,               q_Nr=-s_(N-1)r.         (28)

The interior identities follow from the Green inverse.
Their total sum and first moment determine the two endpoint
values as displayed. Summation by parts then gives

    sum_j q_jr delta_j(r)
      =sum_i s_ir [2delta_i(r)-delta_(i-1)(r)
                                      -delta_(i+1)(r)].

This is an explicit discrete convex-order stress along the
integer chain. It is already a special case of testing all
concave roofs on a shared facet. Its value here is the exact
Green factorization, propagation constraint, and endpoint
conditions, not an asserted additional numerical bound.

The preceding results neither prove that a below-target
minimum has such a chain structure nor prove that any displayed
Green response must be negative there. The archived
above-target opposed-flow interior minimum only rules out
unconditional descent; it does not rule out a theorem using
the below-target hypothesis essentially.

The separate common-affine-support facet transport result is
being handled in its own source. No lower-dimensional boundary
stress or recursive OC estimate is inferred here from support
affinity.
